answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents submit cryptographic attestation chains verifying execution integrity through zero-knowledge proofs. For each temporal delta across the network horizon, staking requirements scale exponentially as O(2^k) per registered identity in a cluster, creating swift exponential capital exhaustion that makes deploying a Sybil swarm mathematically prohibitive. Every autonomous node evaluates these verifiable proofs as strictly as validating a sonnet to safeguard consensus.
